frame: Each GLB is modelled in its airport ENU frame (aeqd about the ARP; x east, y north, z up, metres; ground = airfield datum z 0) and exported +Y up, so three.js gets (x east, y up, z = -north). Place every GLB at the origin with an identity transform. bbox_enu is in ENU.
replaces_note: replaces = layout.json building ids that the model supersedes: hide those extrusions when the GLB is shown.
hierarchy: <name> (root empty, extras: icao, title, replaces) -> LOD0 / LOD1 / LOD2 -> mesh nodes (LOD1/LOD2 node names carry a _LOD1/_LOD2 suffix); one primitive per material

materials.M_GlassLit: same glazing on large lit glazed areas (facades, skylights, tower cabs): make it emissive at night (warm white); not emissive in the GLB
materials.M_Structure: white / light-grey steel arches, ribs, mullions, soffits, canopies
materials.M_Accent: per-asset accent, see material_values (OMSJ: blue ceramic lattice screens, baked texture T_Lattice.png)
materials.M_Dark: soffits in shadow, recesses, louvres, apron-level bands
materials.M_Lights: aviation obstruction lights (red), emissive in the GLB (strength 4)

uv: UVMap: box projection in metres x per-material scale (glass 0.25 /m, roof 0.1 /m, M_Accent 0.4 /m for the lattice texture), relative to each mesh node origin
